messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P0 alert: possible cross-tenant KV reads observed in dedicated pool 'ded-prod-43' (customer: BespokeHealth). Pager: @Evan oncall. Full alert: high rate of `kv.get` with mixed tenant prefixes.
Evan: acked. pulling logs now. which pool is this exactly?
Anita: pool id ded-prod-43, assigned to VPC vh-07, reserved capacity for BespokeHealth (tenant 834). Noted there was a config rollout 3h ago that touched routing-agent.
Sophia: I'm oncall too, joining. Any evidence of reads returning other tenant keys?
Evan: initial grep from audit logs: 
```
2024-05-03T18:02:12Z INFO kv.get key="tenant:834:session:abc123" svc=kv-cache pool=ded-prod-43
2024-05-03T18:02:12Z INFO kv.get key="tenant:4093:session:def456" svc=kv-cache pool=ded-prod-43
2024-05-03T18:02:13Z INFO kv.get key="tenant:834:profile:uid-22" svc=kv-cache pool=ded-prod-43
```
This shows interleaved accesses; need to check whether the responses were returned to wrong tenant.
Sophia: can you paste the response bodies (redacted) for the 4093 request?
Evan: pulling from node logs now. One node (node-7) has mixed shard mappings. snippet: `shard_map[node-7] = {prefixes: [tenant:834, tenant:4093]}` that shouldn't happen.
Anita: we rolled out `routing-agent v2.14.0` to ded-prod-43 3h ago. its change was a fallback merge for prefix resolution to improve cache hit. possibly introduced shared prefix table bug.
Liam: cc @security @customer-success. This is potentially cross-tenant exposure; we need containment first.
Evan: mitigation plan proposal: 1) mark pool ded-prod-43 as draining (stop new requests), 2) attach emergency circuit to route traffic for BespokeHealth to standby pool, 3) snapshot logs and preserve nodes for forensic, 4) roll back routing-agent on nodes where shard_map shows mixed prefixes.
Sophia: agree. I'll set the pool to `draining` and create a temporary rate limit on pool. Doing: `redwoodctl pools update ded-prod-43 --state draining`
ops-bot: command accepted, state change queued.
Evan: starting live migration for BespokeHealth to standby pool ded-standby-9: `redwoodctl migrate --from ded-prod-43 --to ded-standby-9 --tenant 834 --mode immediate`
Anita: initiating rollback of routing-agent on node-7/8/11 where the mismatch appears: `kubectl -n serving rollout undo deployment/routing-agent --to-revision=2 --kube-context=ded-prod-43`
Evan: collecting evidence: audit snapshot exported to s3://incidents/1719876543/evidence.tar.gz (access restricted).
Sophia: quick check — are there any customer-facing errors reported? Support page shows a small uptick in 5xx for BespokeHealth from 18:01 to 18:08. Could be related to draining.
Evan: customer impact summary so far: read semantics may have returned data for tenant 4093 to a BespokeHealth request window 18:02-18:04; volume ~12 hits. We need to treat this as confirmed exposure until proven otherwise.
Liam: started a conference bridge with CS and Legal. CS drafting a customer message template (no admission yet; informing that we're investigating).
Anita: rolling node binaries back completed on node-7 and node-8. node-11 pending due to active sessions, winding down.
Sophia: confirm traffic to ded-standby-9 now for tenant 834. monitoring token-level traces.
Evan: found a commit in routing-agent that accidentally allowed `prefix_glob` to match across tenants when a shared cache key option was present — there's a missing tenant-scoping check in `resolve_prefixes()` (line ~412).
Evan: example repro locally: 
```
# repro snippet
req.prefix = "session:abc123"
if cache_key == "shared:latest":
    resolved = global_prefix_resolver(req.prefix)  # <-- returns both tenant prefixes
```
Sophia: OK that explains mixed shard_map. Priority: block shared cache_key mode until we patch.
Anita: pushed emergency config to disable shared cache keys at runtime: `PATCH /admin/pools/ded-prod-43/config {"allow_shared_cache_keys": false}`. Applying to all nodes.
ops-bot: config patch applied to nodes [node-3,node-4,node-7,node-8,node-11].
Evan: nodes where rollback complete show shard_map corrected. No further interleaved kv.get entries after 18:12 in those nodes.
Sophia: marking incident as contained for live traffic. Still need to confirm full blast radius and whether any other pools got the rollout.
Liam: handoff notes for next oncall (Liam):
- Incident: possible cross-tenant KV reads in ded-prod-43 impacting BespokeHealth (tenant 834).
- Actions taken: pool set to draining, tenant migrated to ded-standby-9, routing-agent rollback on affected nodes, disabled shared cache keys globally for pool, evidence snapshot saved, CS/legal looped.
- Open tasks: forensic review of audit logs (search for `tenant:4093` appearing in `tenant:834` request flows), confirm no other pools received v2.14.0 rollout, timeline and RCA write-up, customer notification draft.
- Contact: Evan (pager), Sophia (SRE), Anita (platform).
Evan: handing pager to @Liam for the next shift — please follow up on the audit and coordinate postmortem.
Liam: taking pager. I'll escalate to security for deeper forensic review (memory dumps + persistent storage check).
Sophia: scheduling a quick blameless RCA kickoff at 09:15 UTC tomorrow; invite: SRE, Platform, Research, CS, Legal.
Anita: root cause (prelim): routing-agent v2.14.0 introduced an opt-in shared cache key path that wasn't tenant-scoped. Patch queued: add tenant guard in resolve_prefixes + unit tests. Target patch deploy to canary tonight.
Evan: customer impact classification: sensitivity: medium-high (possible cross-tenant exposure), affected rows: small (<15), immediate mitigation: complete.
Liam: next steps checklist for oncall:
- complete grep across all pools for mixed tenant prefix traces
- preserve node images for nodes that served mixed responses (don't autoscale them away)
- coordinate with CS/Legal on messaging (no admission until RCA)
- push hotfix to routing-agent and run canary on non-prod then small production canary

Sophia: closing out live pager — status: mitigated for traffic, investigation ongoing. Will update thread when RCA / customer comms ready. :white_check_mark:
Evan: thanks team — nice rapid triage.
Liam: will follow up.
